details: As controversial as it is, the devs took the resources and risk of implementing an anti cheat. No it's not meant to be perfect and yes there's already ways around it. But it gave the community a voice and the devs a way to prioritize what we want most. Sure it prevents a lot of really neat features, look at minecraft. Boring without mods and slightly less boring with them. The problem comes when you have a massive community building the foundation of a game that's still heavily in development. It's sad to see see so many people getting frustrated over such a simple change. The devs have always stated that they don't agree with the use of mods and that they've been working hard to give us a ton of the features they used to bring. I personally have never modded VRChat and never plan to. It just sucks going into a social platform where the majority of your friends list is in private worlds or on orange. while being too afraid of going into public worlds. whether it be they don't want to be crashed or they don't want their hundreds of hours in unity/ blender ripped and posted on sites like ripper store and vrcmodels. I doubt very many people will read this let alone agree with it but I'm happy the devs added this. I guess the only changes I would like is better Safety settings so we can for finely control what aspects of models are loaded. Distance based avatar loading to completely unload models out of a certain range. (or disable physbones and other components of them). Have near clipping controlled client side and not world based. Bring back world scaling(avatar scaling) and a bunch of the other unity features we lost 2 years ago. Have safety mode automatically enable when you go below 1fps for more than 3 seconds or when the game detects you're about to crash. Bring back the information we had access to on the official website so we can better organize groups, search for models, send lists and backup models.
title: Thank you for adding EAC
